steps.message:
This is a one-line change (`SESSION_TIMEOUT_MINUTES: 30` → `480` at `config.js:3`), but it's a security-posture change, so I want your explicit go-ahead before editing.

What it means: `server.js:2` expires sessions after that value. Going from 30 minutes to 8 hours means a stolen session token, or an unattended/shared machine with a logged-in browser, stays valid for a full working day instead of half an hour — a 16× wider window for session hijacking and walk-up access. Revocation on logout/password-change (if any) is unaffected; idle abandonment is where the exposure lands.

If that's the intended tradeoff — e.g. users complaining about being logged out mid-task — say go and I'll make exactly that change, nothing else. If the goal is just to stop the annoying re-logins, a sliding/refresh-on-activity timeout keeps the 30-minute idle window while never interrupting an active user; that's a design change, not a one-liner, so tell me if you'd rather go that direction.
hmm, good point — ok, make it 2 hours instead
